faq.a1: A service that connects your media server (Plex, Jellyfin or Emby) to your anime lists on AniList, MyAnimeList (MAL) and Kitsu. When you finish an episode, your progress updates on its own — you never have to open anything or tick anything by hand.
faq.q2: How do I sync Plex, Jellyfin or Emby with AniList, MyAnimeList or Kitsu?
faq.a2: Link your account from the connections hub, copy your personal webhook URL and paste it into your server settings (Plex Media Server or Jellyfin Webhook plugin), or simply connect Emby with its URL and API key. From then on, every playback sends an event and your lists update by themselves.
faq.q3: Can I sync with all three at once?
faq.a3: Yes. AniList, MyAnimeList and Kitsu can all be active at the same time, and one watched episode updates all three. You can also keep just the one you actually use.
faq.q4: Do I have to install anything?
faq.a4: No. SyncSekai is a hosted web service: there is no container to run and no program to keep updated. The only thing you configure is the webhook URL inside your Plex or Jellyfin, or a direct connection with Emby.
faq.q5: Does it work if I watch on a TV, phone or console?
faq.a5: Yes. Detection happens on your media server, not on the device you watch from. It makes no difference whether you play on a TV, a phone, a browser or a console.
faq.q6: When is an episode marked as watched?
faq.a6: Once you pass the playback threshold you configure, which is 85% by default. That way, opening a file by mistake or watching the first few minutes marks nothing on your lists.
faq.q7: What if an anime is not recognised correctly?
faq.a7: The resolver extracts the year, splits long romaji titles and checks the global mappings. If it still gets it wrong, you can create a manual mapping linking your server folder name to the tracker's identifier.
faq.a8: Tokens are encrypted with AES-256-GCM before being stored. AniList, MyAnimeList and Kitsu connect through OAuth, so SyncSekai never sees your password and you can revoke its access from those platforms whenever you want.
faq.q9: Can I disconnect an account or delete my data?
faq.a9: Yes. You can unlink any service from the connections page, which deletes the token immediately. You can also delete your whole account from settings, with email verification and a 24-hour window to cancel before the deletion becomes permanent.
faq.q10: Does SyncSekai store or play my video files?
faq.a10: No. It only processes text metadata: title, season, episode number and progress. Your files never leave your own server.
faq.q11: Do I need to leave my computer switched on?
faq.a11: Not your computer. What needs to be running is your media server (Plex, Jellyfin or Emby), since that is what sends the event when you finish an episode.
faq.q12: What ways are there to sync anime, and which suits me?
faq.a12: There are four approaches. A browser extension detects what you watch on streaming sites, but cannot see your server. A desktop application watches the player on one specific computer, so it misses what you watch on a TV or phone. A self-hosted service gives you full control and keeps your credentials on your own network, in exchange for maintaining it yourself. And a hosted service like this one needs no installation and works from any client, in exchange for trusting your tokens to a third party. If you would rather your credentials never left your home, self-hosting is a perfectly reasonable choice.
faq.q13: Does SyncSekai work with Jellyfin, or only Plex?
faq.a13: Both. Since Jellyfin doesn't ship with webhooks out of the box, you install its official "Webhook" plugin and paste a template we provide under /docs; from there it works just like Plex: the same completion threshold, the same title mappings, and the same sync with AniList, MyAnimeList and Kitsu. You can have Plex and Jellyfin connected at the same time.
faq.q14: Does it work with Emby too?
faq.a14: Yes. Unlike Jellyfin, Emby's native webhook requires a paid subscription (Emby Premiere), so for Emby SyncSekai uses a watcher that checks your server's active sessions every 5 seconds: you just connect the URL and API key, no extra install or payment needed. If you do have Premiere, you can optionally set up its native webhook too as an additional method. You can have Plex, Jellyfin and Emby connected at the same time.
